arguments.value: This is a cooperation agreement between JANA Partners LLC and URS Corporation. The agreement says JANA beneficially owned 6,745,623 shares of URS common stock when it was signed. URS agreed to expand its board to 14 members at the next board meeting by March 27, 2014, and appoint four JANA nominees as directors, subject to the nominees completing the company’s standard director paperwork and agreeing to company policies. At the 2014 annual meeting, URS agreed to nominate those JANA nominees for election, recommend that shareholders vote for them, use reasonable best efforts to get them elected, and have two existing directors not seek re-election. If a JANA nominee leaves before the 2015 annual meeting, JANA may name a replacement who meets the agreement’s independence and experience requirements. URS also agreed to form a Value Creation Committee, give JANA nominees seats on the CEO succession committee and the compensation committee, and keep the board and certain committees from taking material action before the March board meeting. The company also agreed not to make material new transactions before the March board meeting, and not to increase board size above 12 or reduce it in a way that would force a JANA nominee out before the 2015 annual meeting. JANA agreed to a cooperation and standstill period: it will not disparage URS or its directors, will vote its shares for the board’s nominees, will not run a proxy contest or propose business at the 2014 annual meeting, and will not seek to acquire more than 14.9% of URS common stock or pursue control-related actions without consent. URS likewise agreed not to disparage JANA. The parties agreed to announce the deal in a joint press release by 9:00 a.m. New York City time on March 17, 2014, and JANA would file a Schedule 13D amendment. The agreement is governed by Delaware law. It ends when the cooperation period expires, which is the earlier of 30 days before the deadline for shareholder notice for the 2015 annual meeting under the bylaws or any material breach that is not cured within three business days after notice.
